title: Ὄν, a chant to start
line: Three minutes chanting the Greek word for being.
intro: With Parmenides, Athena holds that only what always is, is: τὸ ὄν, being. Athena chants the word itself and hears in its N the primordial vibration, the One becoming being. Three minutes, before any other sit or on its own.
does: Chant ὄν slowly for three minutes, then rest in the vibration.
trains: A still centre: attention gathered in one sound, then in the silence after it.

steps.text: Sit upright and close your eyes. Let two or three breaths go out a little longer than they come in.
Chant “on”, slowly, on a long out-breath: an open O that closes into N. Breathe in, and chant again, at your own pace.
Keep chanting, and let your attention rest on the N as it vibrates on the palate.
Let the sound stop. Rest in the vibration that stays after it, and in the silence it leaves.
